findings.title: Suspect-issue PR comments call helpers that are not on the workflow class
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `get_environment_info` are defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (the class that ends just before `OpenPRCommentWorkflow`), but `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` call them as `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` / `self.get_environment_info(issue)`. Those workflow classes subclass `PRCommentWorkflow`, which holds an integration rather than inheriting these methods. The static helper also does `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, and `_truncate_title` is not defined on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment therefore raises AttributeError, so the GitHub/GitLab comment task fails and no comment is posted.

findings.title: Flagged table widgets render an empty hardcoded table
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `tableResultComponent` ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, column fields, aliases, and the loading state and instead renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData.data: []`. An empty `columns` array is truthy, so the visualization will not infer columns from meta either. Any org with that flag on sees blank dashboard table widgets instead of the query results.

findings.title: Replay error context reads title/message that stored events do not have
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds the Seer log from `data.get("title")` and `data.get("message")` on the raw nodestore payload. Stored error events usually keep the exception under `exception.values` / `metadata` (`type` and `value`); `title` is computed on the Event model and is often absent, and `message` is frequently empty. The log becomes `User experienced an error: ': ' at ...`, so exception type and value never reach the summary. The new test expects `ZeroDivisionError` and `division by zero` in that log after storing an exception-only event, which this field choice does not produce.

findings.title: Error events are not ordered against replay segment timestamps
findings.body: Chronological merge compares nodestore `timestamp` (unix seconds, and sometimes an ISO-8601 string) with the raw segment event `timestamp`. Recording segments are rrweb payloads whose timestamps are milliseconds. A seconds value is always less than a millisecond timestamp, so every error is emitted before every breadcrumb; if the stored timestamp is a string, `str < float` raises TypeError and the summarize request 500s. That is a regression for replays that have linked errors, because this endpoint previously summarized breadcrumbs without this comparison. The unit test avoids it by fabricating segment timestamps in seconds.

findings.title: Error IDs are queried with page-filter dates the AI tab never sends
findings.body: Error IDs now come from `query_replay_instance` using `start`/`end` from `get_filter_params(request, project)`. Segment loading (`fetch_segments_metadata`) does not use that window. The replay AI tab calls `/replays/{id}/summarize/breadcrumbs/` with no `statsPeriod`, `start`, or `end`. Depending on the default stats period, either the request 400s (breaking an endpoint that previously did not need dates) or error lookup is limited to a window shorter than replay retention, so older replays are summarized with no error context while their breadcrumbs still load.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only inside the `searchQuery` branch. When the search box is empty the function returns `sortAttributes(attributes)` unfiltered, so those fields still render. When the user searches, the same names are excluded even if the query matches them. The hide list needs to apply before the search filter, not instead of the unfiltered list.

findings.title: 60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity refresh batch
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` now has `processing_deadline_duration=60`, but `check_auth` still enqueues up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities and this task refreshes them sequentially via external IdP calls. That routinely exceeds 60s. `check_auth` already sets `last_synced=now` before the task runs, so if the worker kills the task and does not retry the same id list, the unfinished identities are skipped until the next ~24h cycle and SSO validity is not refreshed. If it does retry, the same chunk keeps timing out and hammering the IdP.

findings.title: Report URL validation rejects real browser documents and aborts the batch
findings.body: `url` is a DRF `URLField`, whose default validator only allows http(s)/ftp. Reporting API document URLs include `about:blank`, `blob:`, `chrome-extension:`, and `file:` URLs, so those reports fail validation. The handler then returns 422 on the first invalid item and does not record metrics for any later valid reports in the same array. Browsers post mixed batches, and the previous dataclass path accepted unknown types and non-http URLs and still counted them.

findings.title: Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter
findings.body: The summary request sends the normalized datetime and `selection.projects`, but not `selection.environments`. The feedback list page is wrapped in page filters, so the list and search respect the environment selector while the summary does not. A user filtered to one environment still gets a summary of feedback from every environment in the project/date range, which can contradict the list beside it.

findings.title: Trace waterfall wrapper dropped height: 100%
findings.body: The waterfall root was a flex column with `flex-grow: 1` and `height: 100%`. It is now `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`, which does not set `height: 100%`. The trace view sizes this pane with a height chain rather than only flex-grow, so the waterfall can collapse and the virtualized span tree no longer fills the viewport.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers cannot return falsy nodes
findings.body: Both head and body renderers treat any falsy return as "use the fallback" (`if (cell)`), but the documented contract is that only `undefined` means fallback. A custom renderer that returns `0`, `''`, or `null` (valid React output, and a reasonable way to blank a cell) is discarded and the default field renderer runs instead.
